With a more pronounced herbal character than other contenders, Stove Top Traditional Sage leans hard into classic Thanksgiving flavors.

Why it won us over: This was one of the most visually appealing stuffings we tasted, with plenty of browned, crunchy bits. But its seasoning really distinguished it. While several competitors tasted quite mild, this one had an assertive sage flavor (no surprise there) backed by a buttery note that reminded some tasters of movie-theater popcorn.
Best for: Sage lovers—or anyone who wants a stuffing mix sturdy enough to repurpose. Serve it as is, spoon it into stuffed mushrooms, or toast the dry mix into stuffing-flavored breadcrumbs.

Pepperidge Farm Herb-Seasoned Classic Stuffing requires a little more work than the other mixes we tested: You supply the onion, celery, and chicken stock. But that effort pays off in a stuffing with more varied texture and fresher flavor.

Why it won us over: Fresh celery gave the stuffing welcome crunch, while rosemary and thyme supplied classic holiday flavor. A subtle sweetness rounded things out. It stood well apart from Pepperidge Farm’s cornbread version, which we found gummy and grainy.

Best for: Cooks who don’t mind a little chopping in exchange for a more homemade result. You can also skip the celery and onions and use the dry mix as a binder for turkey meatballs or as seasoned breading for fried fish.
BUY IT: Pepperidge Farm Herb-Seasoned Classic Stuffing, 12-oz. bag; $4 at Amazon
How we tested

We prepared all seven stuffing mixes according to their package directions. Most called for water or broth and butter; mixes that required additional ingredients were prepared with those ingredients as directed. Brand names were concealed during the tasting, and editors evaluated each stuffing for flavor, texture, and appearance.
What we looked for
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/66a2de7357c82043fa7922ad/1:1/w_90%2Cc_limit/sam-stone_061224_2919_VOG_final.jpg

The best boxed stuffing should be fluffy and tender inside with crisp, golden-brown edges. We favored mixes with distinct pieces of bread that absorbed liquid without becoming gummy or soggy. Flavor-wise, we looked for buttery savoriness and recognizable Thanksgiving herbs like sage, rosemary, and parsley.
Other boxed stuffing mixes we tried
Kroger Chicken-Flavored Stuffing Mix: Light and airy with good structure, but too mild for our tastes.
Trader Joe’s Corn Bread Stuffing Mix: Soggy and nearly liquidy, without enough flavor to compensate for the texture.
Pepperidge Farm Corn Bread Classic Stuffing: Both gummy and grainy, with muted seasoning.
Whole Foods Traditional Stuffing Mix: Mushy, with cracked rye seeds that stuck in our teeth and a peppery flavor that overwhelmed the traditional herbs.
How to make boxed stuffing taste better

Boxed stuffing is easy to upgrade. First, if your mix calls for water, swap it out for chicken or turkey stock for a more savory flavor. Add sautéed onion, celery, or carrots; cooked sausage; or toasted nuts for extra texture. Dried cranberries or raisins bring sweetness, while a handful of fresh herbs perks up the flavor.

For a richer, more cohesive stuffing, stir in a couple of beaten eggs and bake the mixture in a casserole dish until fluffy inside and crisp on top. Or leave well enough alone—our favorite boxed stuffing tastes pretty great straight from the package.
Editor’s note: This review of stuffing mixes was first published in November 2023; it has been updated for style and content.
